messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: multiple egress path deviations observed from ashburn-azb to upstream transit providers. Severity: P2. Affected: outbound traffic to provider-carrierX (AS64500). Potential customer impact: intermittent packetloss to EU/West regions. Paging oncall.
oncall-net: Ack. I'm on it, pulling BGP adjacencies and metrics. ETA 2m.
sre-alex: Seeing spikes in retransmits for a subset of prefixes out of ashburn, correlates with provider-carrierX. Ping loss ~5-7% since 00:42 UTC.
net-team-lead-maria: @oncall-net if carrier looks flappy we should prepare to shift egress to carrierY for critical prefixes. Have we hit any traffic shift runbooks recently? :thinking_face:
oncall-net: Runbook: ashburn-egress-failover. Starting checks: neighbor state, RIB groups, MED/LP changes.
oncall-net: Running: ```show ip bgp summary | include 64500
64500         192.0.2.10      4d 02:12    1       0      0  Established
a64500        192.0.2.11      00:41       2       7      0  Active
``` Looks like one session with carrierX (192.0.2.11) flapping, other is fine. Also seeing more AS path prepends inbound from carrierX.
sre-alex: grabbing tcpdump on egress spine to confirm packet loss pattern. If session flips, we may see microbursts of RSTs to clients. Also verifying prefix set impacted: 198.51.100.0/22 and 203.0.113.0/24 are top talkers to EU.
eng-ops-jamie: FYI build triggering for dedicated customers in ashburn won't failover automatically to carrierY unless we flip route export policies. Need manual step.
support-ivy: Notifying tier2 support and prepping CNAs for customers in EU reporting latency/failed requests. Do we have estimated impacted customer list?
net-team-lead-maria: @support-ivy primary impacted customers: 3 enterprise tenants using Dedicated in ashburn and a subset of Hosted traffic hitting carrierX paths. Can we post a quick status update? Keep it factual: network egress instability to carrierX, mitigation in progress.
oncall-net: Contacting carrierX NOC now. initial cURL: ```curl -X POST https://noc.carrierx.example/api/incidents -d '{"site":"ashburn","symptom":"bgp adjacency jitter","priority":"high"}'``` (placeholder)
carrierx-noc: (automated) Received. Investigating potential upstream route flaps and partial blackholing. We see a control-plane process restart at our edge at 00:41 UTC, looking into hardware vs software.
sre-alex: We can mitigate quickly by withdrawing selective prefixes to carrierX and preferring carrierY via local-pref changes for critical prefixes. Proposing two-phase: 1) adjust local-preference for prefix-set critical-egress to prefer carrierY; 2) if no improvement, withdraw community export to carrierX and announce more-specifics to carrierY.
eng-ops-jamie: +1 on two-phase. Requesting change window doc: small-impact, target 00:55 UTC now. Who will run the BGP policy change?
oncall-net: I'll apply policy now on ashburn-egress-router-1. Command: ```conf t
route-map PREFER-CARRIERY permit 10
 set local-preference 200
exit
route-map APPLY-CRITICAL permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list CRITICAL-EGRESS
 set local-preference 200
exit
router bgp 64510
 neighbor 192.0.2.20 route-map APPLY-CRITICAL out
``` Applying to neighbor 192.0.2.20 (carrierY) and corresponding out to make sure it takes precedence.
net-team-lead-maria: Keep me posted. Also start mitigation notice to support channel and add to public status page draft.
sre-alex: After applying policy, observing immediate shift: traffic for 198.51.100.0/22 -> carrierY. Packetloss dropped from 6% -> 0.5% for that prefix. Good sign.
support-ivy: Posting status: "We are experiencing degraded egress to some endpoints from our Ashburn region due to an upstream provider issue. We have applied routing mitigations; we are monitoring for recovery."
pm-ryan: Please include ETA note — when do we expect full resolution vs longer term fix? Customers asking.
carrierx-noc: Followup: we confirmed a cooling fan failure triggered a failover to hot-standby, causing control-plane instability at one POP. Reboot sequence in progress. Estimated repair 35m.
oncall-net: Thanks. We'll keep local-pref mitigation active for critical prefixes until carrierX confirms stability. Rolling back will be manual once they confirm.
sre-alex: Running continuous checks and collecting pcap for postmortem. Dumping small capture snippet: ```tcpdump -n -r egress-ashburn.pcap | head -n 20
00:42:11.123 IP 198.51.100.10 > 93.184.216.34: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
00:42:11.125 IP 198.51.100.10 > 93.184.216.34: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240 (retrans)
00:42:11.221 IP 198.51.100.10 > 93.184.216.34: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240 (retrans)
``` shows retrans pattern during adj jitter window.
net-team-lead-maria: Good capture. Add to incident timeline. We'll include root cause once carrier confirms hardware cause. Marking P2 -> may escalate if customer impact grows.
support-ivy: Customers reached out, some reported retries and higher latency. No data plane errors beyond what we've seen. SLA impact for dedicated tenants: minor but needs accurate PR and SRE follow-up.
oncall-net: Keeping policy in place. Will start a 10m watch and then evaluate rollback with carrier confirmation.
carrierx-noc: Update: control-plane stable, bgp sessions re-established at 01:18 UTC. We're continuing post-reboot checks. Please verify from your side and advise if you want us to clear session.
sre-alex: Verified stabilization from our side. Sessions show Established and routes consistent. Observed no packetloss for last 10 mins. Reverting local-pref in 5m after final checks to avoid route churn.
eng-ops-jamie: Note for postmortem: add runbook timing, who executed policy, and sample commands. Also include steps to automate temporary egress preference for these classes of failures.
net-team-lead-maria: Thanks everyone. Final action: @oncall-net to document commands and timeline, @support-ivy to send customers a follow-up, @pm-ryan to update incident page. I'll schedule a quick RCA sync at 09:00 UTC.
oncall-net: Documenting now. Closing incident thread once postmortem created. :white_check_mark:
